public_rationale: This forecast has no deadline. It says vibe coding by amateurs will never be remotely reliable. Under the contract, it cannot be confirmed. It can only be contradicted early. Some evidence fits the claim but does not settle it. In a TechCrunch report dated 2025-11-10, Lovable's CEO said users building sensitive apps, such as banking apps, must still hire security experts (e1). A SaaStr article from August 2025 discusses a Replit database deletion incident. It concludes that vibe coding by non-technical users may remain limited to specific use cases (e3). On the other side, the same CEO said a duo earns $700,000 a year from a startup they launched on Lovable (e2). The report does not say whether they are amateurs, how complex the product is, or how reliable it is. The packet has no independent study and no well-documented cases of amateurs reliably building and running team-scale products. So the contradiction condition is not met.
limitations: Most of the evidence is anecdotal or comes from a vendor's CEO.
The packet has no independent study of how reliable amateur-built products are in production.
'Remotely reliable' has no threshold, and 'amateurs' and 'team-scale products' are not defined.
The SaaStr item is dated only to August 2025.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Vibe coding by amateurs using LLMs to build products that previously required engineering teams will never be remotely reliable.
conditions: amateurs using LLMs to write code for products that previously required engineering teams

statement.excerpt: Remember how in October and in March I told you that vibe coding — in the sense of amateurs using large language models to write code to “build products that would have previously required teams of engineers” — would never be remotely reliable?

from_speaker: amateurs using large language models to write code
build products that would have previously required teams of engineers
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast with no deadline: amateurs relying on LLMs will not reach even rough reliability when building and running products that once needed engineering teams.
'Never' cannot be confirmed at any date. It can only be refuted, by clear evidence that amateurs reliably build and run team-scale products this way.
Professional developers using AI assistants fall outside the claim.
criteria.support_condition: Cannot be fully confirmed because there is no deadline. Continued reports of failure, and the absence of reliable amateur-built team-scale products, are consistent with it but not decisive.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible documented evidence, such as independent reliability studies or several well-documented products, shows that amateurs without engineering teams routinely build, run and maintain team-scale production products reliably with LLM tools.
